what_its_for: Selexipag is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the arteries that carry blood to your lungs. It helps keep these blood vessels open and relaxed so your heart does not have to work as hard. This medicine can slow down the worsening of PAH and reduce the chance of being hospitalized.
how_to_take: Take selexipag by mouth with food, as food helps reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, split, or chew them. Take it twice a day, about 12 hours apart (for example, morning and evening). Try to take it at the same times every day to keep an even level of medicine in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose (200 mcg twice a day) and slowly increase it every week by 200 mcg until you reach the highest dose that works for you without causing too many side effects. The maximum dose is 1,600 mcg twice a day. Do not change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions. If you have liver problems, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose or ask you to take it only once a day.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is more than 6 hours before your next scheduled dose. If it is less than 6 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss doses for 3 or more days in a row, contact your doctor before restarting, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
storage: Store selexipag at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from moisture and heat. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the medicine in its original packaging and out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking selexipag with gemfibrozil (a cholesterol medicine) as this combination greatly increases the level of selexipag in your blood and can cause serious side effects. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take. Avoid becoming pregnant while on this medicine, as it may harm an unborn baby — use reliable birth control. Limit or avoid alcohol, as it may worsen side effects like low blood pressure and dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe headaches that do not go away, jaw pain or pain in your arms or legs (especially with walking), signs of low blood pressure such as dizziness, fainting, or feeling lightheaded, unusual or severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting, shortness of breath that suddenly gets worse, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing, or if you are planning to become pregnant or think you may be pregnant.
when_it_works: Selexipag starts working right away in your body, but you may not feel better immediately. It can take several weeks to months before you notice improvements in your symptoms, such as being able to walk farther or feeling less short of breath. It is very important to keep taking this medicine even if you feel well, as it is working to slow down the progression of your disease. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine may harm an unborn baby. If you are able to become pregnant, use effective birth control during treatment and talk to your doctor about your options. Breastfeeding: It is not known if selexipag passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Selexipag is approved for adults and children 8 years and older who weigh at least 40 kg (about 88 pounds). Liver problems: If you have moderate liver disease, your doctor will likely reduce your dose. If you have severe liver disease, this medicine should not be used. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for kidney problems. Older adults: No special dose changes are needed based on age alone, but your doctor will monitor you closely.
